record.paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
record.original_question: How can the iterative reconstruction algorithms used for LINC-NIRVANA multiple-image deconvolution be accelerated in a mathematically justified and computationally efficient way? The target algorithms include Richardson-Lucy and ordered-subsets expectation-maximization variants for large astronomical images, where sufficiently bright objects can require thousands of iterations and 2048 x 2048 pixel images can take hours; existing acceleration methods need convergence guarantees and better behavior in critical cases.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $g_1, \dots, g_p$ be observed images on a discrete pixel grid (e.g., $2048 \times 2048$), modeling photon counts from a common non-negative object $f \ge 0$ through linear imaging operators $A_j$ (typically convolutions with known point-spread functions $h_j$) plus Poisson noise:
$$ g_j \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(A_j f + b_j), \qquad j = 1,\dots,p, $$
where $b_j \ge 0$ are known backgrounds. The multiple-image Richardson–Lucy (RL) iteration for maximum-likelihood reconstruction is
$$ f^{(k+1)} = \frac{f^{(k)}}{\sum_{j=1}^p A_j^{*} \mathbf{1}} \sum_{j=1}^p A_j^{*}\!\left( \frac{g_j}{A_j f^{(k)} + b_j} \right), $$
and the ordered-subsets expectation-maximization (OSEM) variant replaces the sum over $j$ by a cyclic sweep through subsets of the data, accelerating per-iteration progress by roughly a factor $p$ but losing the monotone-likelihood and convergence guarantees of RL.

Problem. Construct an acceleration scheme for the multiple-image RL iteration (and its regularized variants) that
(i) provably converges to a maximizer of the Poisson log-likelihood (or of the regularized objective), 
(ii) achieves a substantial speed-up over standard RL on instances requiring thousands of iterations on large ($\sim 2048 \times 2048$) images, and
(iii) behaves robustly in critical regimes where existing accelerators (such as OSEM, vector-extrapolation, or adaptive step-length methods) lose monotonicity, stall, or diverge.

Specifically: provide an iterative algorithm together with a proof of convergence, an analysis of its asymptotic rate, and a characterization of the parameter choices that guarantee stable acceleration uniformly over realistic object/PSF configurations encountered in Fizeau interferometric imaging.
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple partial results exist: scaled-gradient-projection (SGP) methods and block-iterative Richardson–Lucy schemes have been proposed with convergence guarantees and significant speed-ups over standard RL/OSEM, while adaptive accelerated Lucy–Richardson variants exist without full convergence proofs. A general acceleration with provable convergence that uniformly handles all critical regimes for LINC-NIRVANA-scale multiple-image deconvolution does not appear to be fully established, so the problem is best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Efficient deconvolution methods for astronomical imaging: algorithms and IDL-GPU codes
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates multiple-image RL, OSEM acceleration and regularized variants in the LINC-NIRVANA context.
status_evidence.claim: Acceleration via OSEM gives a factor-p speed-up but lacks the convergence guarantees of RL.

status_evidence.title: Block-iterative Richardson-Lucy methods for image deblurring
status_evidence.snippet: Block-iterative RL methods are introduced with convergence analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial progress: block-iterative RL with convergence properties.

status_evidence.title: An Adaptively Accelerated Lucy-Richardson Method for Image Deblurring
status_evidence.snippet: Adaptive acceleration of LR without complete convergence theory.
status_evidence.claim: Heuristic accelerations exist but lack full theoretical convergence guarantees.

status_evidence.title: Noise amplification and ill-convergence of Richardson-Lucy deconvolution
status_evidence.snippet: Recent study of RL convergence pathologies.
status_evidence.claim: Critical behavior of RL remains an active research topic.
